docs.title: marktripy
docs.text:
marktripy turns Markdown text into a tree of Python objects, lets you change that tree, and writes it back out as Markdown or HTML. The PyPI package is called marktripy; the source lives in the vexyart/vexy-marktripy repository.

from marktripy.core.parser import ParserRegistry
from marktripy.parsers import markdown_it  # importing the module registers the parser
from marktripy.renderers.markdown import MarkdownRenderer

parser = ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it")
doc = parser.parse("# Hello\n\nThis is **bold** text.\n")

for node in doc.find_all("heading"):
    node.level += 1

print(MarkdownRenderer().render(doc))
# ## Hello
#
# This is **bold** text.

docs.title: What the package does
docs.text:
Every operation follows the same three stages:

  1. Parse. A parser adapter reads Markdown text and builds a Document node. Two adapters ship with the package: one built on markdown-it-py and one built on mistletoe.
  2. Change. You edit the tree directly, or you run transformers (heading level changes, heading IDs, a table of contents, reference-style links) and extensions (strikethrough, task lists, ++key++ keyboard notation).
  3. Render. A renderer walks the tree and produces text. MarkdownRenderer writes Markdown, HTMLRenderer writes HTML.

All three stages share one node model, described in The AST. Because both parsers produce the same node types, a transformer or renderer does not need to know which parser built the tree.

docs.title: Project status
docs.text:
The package is at an early stage (Development Status :: 3 - Alpha in pyproject.toml). The core parse → change → render loop works and is covered by the test suite, but some parts are incomplete:

  • There is no top-level convenience API. You import classes from their modules, for example marktripy.core.parser.ParserRegistry. The names parse_markdown, render_markdown and markdown_to_html shown in older README examples do not exist.
  • There is no command-line tool.
  • Several behaviours have known gaps, for example table bodies from the markdown-it adapter and [[TOC]] marker replacement. See Known limitations before you rely on a feature.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
Markdown text
   │  Parser.preprocess()        normalise line endings, add final newline
   ▼
backend tokens  (markdown-it-py tokens or mistletoe tokens)
   │  adapter conversion         one ASTNode per supported token
   ▼
Document (ASTNode tree)
   │  Parser.postprocess()
   │  ExtensionManager.apply_ast_transformations()   optional
   │  Transformer.transform() / TransformerChain     optional
   │  direct edits                                   optional
   ▼
Document (changed)
   │  Renderer.render()          dispatch on node.type
   ▼
Markdown or HTML text

The tree is the only thing that passes between stages. A parser does not know which renderer will be used, and a renderer does not know which parser built the tree.

docs.title: Design decisions
docs.text:
One node model for every backend. Both parser adapters convert their backend's tokens into the same ASTNode classes. Transformers, extensions, the validator and renderers are written once against those classes. The cost is that anything an adapter does not convert is lost; see Known limitations.

Dispatch on the type string. Renderers call render_<type>, transformers call visit_<type> and the validator calls _validate_<type>. New node types therefore need no changes to the core: create a node with a new type and add a method with the matching name. Extensions rely on this when they attach render_keyboard_key or render_strikethrough to a renderer instance.

Registries filled on import. ParserRegistry and RendererRegistry are class-level dictionaries. Each adapter or renderer module registers itself at the bottom of the file, so a name is available only after its module has been imported. TransformerRegistry exists but nothing registers into it by default.

Configuration as plain dictionaries. Every parser, renderer, transformer and extension takes an optional config dictionary and reads keys with defaults. Unknown keys are ignored, so a misspelt key fails silently. The tables on each page list the keys the code actually reads.

Extensions work after parsing. The shipped extensions find their syntax by inspecting the finished tree (for example, searching text nodes for ++…++) rather than by adding tokenizer rules. This keeps them independent of the backend, but it means they only see syntax that survived parsing as text.

Logging off by default. Every module logs through loguru at debug or info level. The package disables its logger on import so library users see nothing unless they call logger.enable("marktripy").

docs.title: Background research
docs.text: The ref/ directory in the repository holds the research notes that led to this design: ref1.md, ref2.md and ref3.md compare Python Markdown libraries (markdown, markdown2, mistune, marko, markdown-it-py, mistletoe and others) on AST access, extensibility and round-trip support.

docs.title: The AST
docs.text: All parsers produce, and all transformers and renderers consume, the same tree of ASTNode objects defined in marktripy/core/ast.py.

docs.title: The base class
docs.text:
ASTNode is a dataclass with five fields:

Field Type Default Meaning type str required Node kind, such as "heading" or "text". An empty string raises ValueError. children list[ASTNode] [] Child nodes, in document order attrs dict[str, Any] {} Attributes. HTMLRenderer writes most of them as HTML attributes. content str \| None None Text for leaf nodes (text, inline_code, code_block) meta dict[str, Any] {} Free space for parser- or tool-specific data. Nothing in the package reads it.

The type string drives dispatch everywhere: renderers call render_<type>, transformers call visit_<type>, and the validator calls _validate_<type>. A node you create with ASTNode(type="callout") is therefore a valid node; a renderer only needs a render_callout method to output it.

docs.title: Tree methods
docs.text:
Method What it does add_child(child) Appends child to children. remove_child(child) Removes child. Raises ValueError if it is not a child. replace_child(old, new) Puts new in the position of old. Raises ValueError if old is not a child. get_attr(name, default=None) Reads attrs[name]. set_attr(name, value) Writes attrs[name]. walk() Returns a list of this node and all descendants, depth first, parent before children. find_all(node_type) Returns every node in walk() whose type equals node_type. clone() Returns a deep copy of the subtree. attrs and meta are copied one level deep.

Nodes do not store a reference to their parent. To find a parent, search from the root: next(n for n in root.walk() if child in n.children).

walk() builds the full list before returning it, so it is safe to change node attributes while you loop over it. If you add or remove children during the loop, the loop still visits the nodes that existed when walk() was called.

docs.title: Node classes
docs.text:
Each concrete class fixes type and adds typed fields. The constructors also copy some fields into attrs so that HTMLRenderer can write them.

Class type Extra fields (constructor arguments) Copied into attrs Document document — — Heading heading level=1 (must be 1–6, else ValueError) — Paragraph paragraph — — Text text content (required) — Emphasis emphasis — — Strong strong — — Link link href="", title=None href, and title if set Image image src="", alt="", title=None src, alt, and title if set CodeBlock code_block content (required), language=None language if set InlineCode inline_code content (required) — List list ordered=False, start=None, tight=True start if it is not None and not 1 ListItem list_item — — BlockQuote blockquote — — HorizontalRule horizontal_rule — — Table table — — TableRow table_row — — TableCell table_cell header=False, align=None align if set

All constructors also accept the base-class keyword arguments children, attrs and meta, and content where it is not already required.

Extensions add two more node types, strikethrough and keyboard_key, and the task-list attributes task and checked on list_item nodes. See Extensions.

Typed fields and attrs are separate

Link.href and attrs["href"] start out equal, but changing one does not update the other. HTMLRenderer.render_link reads node.href; MarkdownRenderer.render_link also reads node.href. Change the field, not the attribute.

docs.title: Build a tree by hand
docs.text:
You do not need a parser to create a document:

from marktripy.core.ast import CodeBlock, Document, Heading, Paragraph, Strong, Text
from marktripy.renderers.markdown import MarkdownRenderer

doc = Document()

heading = Heading(level=2)
heading.add_child(Text("Install"))
doc.add_child(heading)

para = Paragraph()
para.add_child(Text("Run "))
bold = Strong()
bold.add_child(Text("uv"))
para.add_child(bold)
doc.add_child(para)

doc.add_child(CodeBlock("uv add marktripy\n", language="bash"))

print(MarkdownRenderer().render(doc))

Output:

## Install

Run **uv**

```bash
uv add marktripy
```

docs.title: Common edits
docs.text:
Lower every heading by one level, stopping at level 6:

for h in doc.find_all("heading"):
    h.level = min(h.level + 1, 6)

Replace every link target that starts with http://:

for link in doc.find_all("link"):
    if link.href.startswith("http://"):
        link.href = "https://" + link.href[len("http://"):]

Collect the plain text of a node with extract_text from marktripy.utils.slugify:

from marktripy.utils.slugify import extract_text

titles = [extract_text(h) for h in doc.find_all("heading")]

Remove all images:

for parent in doc.walk():
    parent.children = [c for c in parent.children if c.type != "image"]

Make an independent copy before a destructive change:

backup = doc.clone()

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Prerequisites: Git, uv, and a clone of https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-marktripy. The default branch is master.

docs.title: Set up the environment
docs.text:
uv sync --dev

This creates .venv/, installs the package in editable mode and adds the dev dependency group (pytest, pytest-benchmark, pytest-cov, hypothesis, mypy, ruff, black, twine, hatch).

docs.title: Run the tests
docs.text:
uv run pytest -q

The suite lives in tests/:

File Covers test_basic.py Parser registration, HTML rendering, AST methods test_roundtrip.py Markdown → AST → Markdown test_transformers.py Heading, ID and TOC transformers test_gfm_extensions.py Strikethrough, task lists, the GFM bundle test_kbd_extension.py ++key++ parsing and rendering test_hypothesis.py Property-based tests with hypothesis test_benchmark.py Timing benchmarks with pytest-benchmark

Skip the benchmarks for a faster run. -k matches test and file names, so this deselects everything in test_benchmark.py:

uv run pytest -q -k "not benchmark"

hatch environments are also configured. uvx hatch test runs the suite in hatch's test environment, and hatch run test:no-benchmark runs pytest -k 'not benchmark'.

docs.title: Lint and type-check
docs.text:
uv run ruff check src tests
uv run ruff format --check src tests
uv run mypy src/marktripy

ruff and black use a line length of 100. mypy is configured with strict = true.

docs.title: Build the package
docs.text:
./build.sh package

This removes dist/, runs uv build and checks the result with twine check. The version comes from the latest Git tag through hatch-vcs; the build writes it to src/marktripy/_version.py, which is ignored by Git. Between tags the version has a development suffix such as 1.0.5.dev1+g<commit>.

docs.title: Build the documentation
docs.text:
The documentation sources are the Markdown files in src_docs/md/. The configuration is src_docs/mkdocs.yml. The site is built with ProperDocs and the MaterialX theme into docs/, which GitHub Pages serves at https://vexy.dev/vexy-marktripy/.

  1. Edit or add pages in src_docs/md/. Add new pages to nav in src_docs/mkdocs.yml.

  2. Preview the site while you edit:

    src_docs/build.sh serve

    The preview runs at http://127.0.0.1:8000.

  3. Run the strict build. It fails on any warning, such as a broken link or a page missing from nav:

    ./build.sh docs

  4. Commit both src_docs/ and the regenerated docs/.

On every push to master that touches src_docs/, the Docs workflow (.github/workflows/docs.yml) rebuilds docs/ and commits the result.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
./publish.sh releases to PyPI:

  1. uvx gitnextver commits pending changes, creates the next vX.Y.Z tag and pushes.
  2. The script stops if HEAD has no vX.Y.Z tag.
  3. ./build.sh package builds and checks dist/.
  4. uv publish dist/* uploads. It needs a credential such as UV_PUBLISH_TOKEN in the environment.

Pushing the tag also starts the Release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml). It builds the package, creates a GitHub release with the files, and uploads to PyPI with twine upload --skip-existing, so it does not fail when publish.sh already uploaded that version.

docs.title: Where to help
docs.text: The Known limitations page lists confirmed defects, each with a reproduction. Fixing one of them, with a test, is the most useful contribution.

docs.title: Extensions
docs.text:
An extension bundles three optional pieces of behaviour for one feature:

  1. an AST transformation that runs after parsing (transform_ast),
  2. a render method for HTML (register_html_renderer),
  3. a render method for Markdown (register_markdown_renderer).

The shipped extensions do all their work in these hooks. They do not add tokenizer rules: the register_inline_rule and register_block_rule hooks exist on the base class but the shipped extensions only log a message there.

Extension Module Name Syntax StrikethroughExtension marktripy.extensions.strikethrough strikethrough ~~text~~ TaskListExtension marktripy.extensions.tasklist tasklist - [ ] item, - [x] item KbdExtension marktripy.extensions.kbd kbd ++key++ GFMExtension marktripy.extensions.gfm gfm Strikethrough plus task lists

docs.title: Use extensions
docs.text:
ExtensionManager (in marktripy.extensions.base) holds a set of extensions and applies them in registration order.

Prerequisites: a parser and the renderers you plan to use.

  1. Create the parser. Use the default preset if you need strikethrough or tables:

    from marktripy.core.parser import ParserRegistry
from marktripy.parsers import markdown_it

parser = ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it", {"preset": "default"})

  2. Register the extensions:

    from marktripy.extensions.base import ExtensionManager
from marktripy.extensions.gfm import GFMExtension
from marktripy.extensions.kbd import KbdExtension

manager = ExtensionManager()
manager.register(GFMExtension())
manager.register(KbdExtension())

  3. Attach the render methods to each renderer instance. The second argument is "html" or "markdown":

    from marktripy.renderers.html import HTMLRenderer
from marktripy.renderers.markdown import MarkdownRenderer

html = HTMLRenderer()
md = MarkdownRenderer()
manager.apply_renderer_extensions(html, "html")
manager.apply_renderer_extensions(md, "markdown")

  4. Parse, then run the AST transformations, then render:

    doc = parser.parse("Press ++Enter++. ~~old~~ new.\n\n- [ ] todo\n- [x] done\n")
doc = manager.apply_ast_transformations(doc)

print(html.render(doc))
print(md.render(doc))

The HTML output:

<p>Press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. <del>old</del> new.</p>
<ul>
<li><input type="checkbox" disabled> todo</li><li><input type="checkbox" disabled checked> done</li></ul>

The Markdown output round-trips the extension syntax:

Press ++Enter++. ~~old~~ new.

- [ ] todo
- [x] done

If you skip step 3, the renderer has no method for the new node types: HTMLRenderer writes <!-- Unknown node type: keyboard_key --> and MarkdownRenderer drops the node. If you skip step 4, the ++key++ text and the [ ] prefixes stay as plain text.

docs.title: Manager methods
docs.text: Method What it does register(extension) Adds the extension and calls its setup(). Raises ValueError if the name is taken or a dependency from get_dependencies() is not registered yet. unregister(name) Calls teardown() and removes the extension. Raises KeyError if unknown, ValueError if another extension depends on it. get(name) Returns the registered extension. Raises KeyError if unknown. list_extensions() Returns the names in load order. apply_parser_extensions(parser) Calls register_inline_rule and register_block_rule on every extension. apply_ast_transformations(ast) Calls transform_ast on every extension, feeding each result to the next, and returns the final tree. apply_renderer_extensions(renderer, format="html") Calls register_html_renderer or register_markdown_renderer on every extension.

docs.title: Strikethrough
docs.text: The markdown-it adapter turns ~~text~~ into a generic node of type strikethrough when the preset supports it (default, not commonmark). StrikethroughExtension.transform_ast replaces each generic node with a Strikethrough instance (same type string, same children). The render methods output <del>…</del> and ~~…~~.

docs.title: Task lists
docs.text:
TaskListExtension.transform_ast looks at the first text of each list item. If it matches [ ], [x] or [X] followed by whitespace, the extension:

  • sets attrs["task"] = True and attrs["checked"] to True or False,
  • removes the [ ] / [x] prefix from the text.

The HTML method writes <li><input type="checkbox" disabled> …</li> (adding checked for done items). The Markdown method writes [ ] … or [x] … after the list marker. Items without the prefix are rendered by the renderer's original render_list_item.

You do not need the tasklists parser plugin for this; the extension works on the plain list text.

docs.title: Keyboard keys
docs.text:
KbdExtension.transform_ast searches every text node for the pattern ++…++ and splits the node into text and KeyboardKey nodes (type keyboard_key). The key text is in node.key.

HTML output is <kbd>key</kbd>. Markdown output is ++key++.

The pattern does not allow + inside the key, so ++Ctrl+C++ is left as text. Write key combinations as separate keys: ++Ctrl++ + ++C++ gives <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>C</kbd>.

docs.title: GFM bundle
docs.text: GFMExtension creates a StrikethroughExtension and a TaskListExtension internally and forwards every hook to both. Register it instead of the two separate extensions; registering both would apply them twice. Tables are not part of the bundle because the parser handles them (with the default preset).

docs.title: Write your own extension
docs.text:
Subclass Extension, implement get_name() and get_description(), and override the hooks you need. This extension turns ==text== inside text nodes into a mark node:

import re

from marktripy.core.ast import ASTNode, Text
from marktripy.extensions.base import Extension

PATTERN = re.compile(r"==([^=]+)==")


class MarkExtension(Extension):
    def get_name(self) -> str:
        return "mark"

    def get_description(self) -> str:
        return "Highlight text written as ==text=="

    def transform_ast(self, ast: ASTNode) -> ASTNode:
        for node in ast.walk():
            new_children = []
            for child in node.children:
                if isinstance(child, Text) and child.content and PATTERN.search(child.content):
                    pos = 0
                    for m in PATTERN.finditer(child.content):
                        if m.start() > pos:
                            new_children.append(Text(child.content[pos:m.start()]))
                        new_children.append(ASTNode(type="mark", children=[Text(m.group(1))]))
                        pos = m.end()
                    if pos < len(child.content):
                        new_children.append(Text(child.content[pos:]))
                else:
                    new_children.append(child)
            node.children = new_children
        return ast

    def register_html_renderer(self, renderer) -> None:
        renderer.render_mark = lambda node: f"<mark>{renderer.render_children(node)}</mark>"

    def register_markdown_renderer(self, renderer) -> None:
        renderer.render_mark = lambda node: f"=={renderer.render_children(node)}=="

Points to follow:

  • Attach render methods to the renderer instance you received, as render_<type>. The renderers look methods up by name at render time.
  • To change how an existing node type renders, keep a reference to the old method and call it for the cases you do not handle. TaskListExtension does this with render_list_item.
  • Return a list of names from get_dependencies() if your extension needs another one registered first.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 or later (requires-python = ">=3.12" in pyproject.toml).
  • The runtime dependencies are installed automatically:
Package Used for markdown-it-py[linkify,plugins] The markdown-it parser adapter and its optional plugins (front matter, footnotes, definition lists, task lists, attributes) mistletoe The mistletoe parser adapter loguru Debug logging (disabled by default) fire, rich Declared dependencies; the package does not currently use them

docs.title: Install from PyPI
docs.text:
With uv in a project:

uv add marktripy

With pip:

pip install marktripy

The package has no command-line entry point, so tools such as pipx that install applications are not useful here.

docs.title: Check the installation
docs.text:
Run this one-liner. It imports the package, registers the markdown-it parser and parses one heading:

python -c "import marktripy; from marktripy.core.parser import ParserRegistry; from marktripy.parsers import markdown_it; print(marktripy.__version__, ParserRegistry.create('markdown-it').parse('# Hi').children[0].type)"

The output is the installed version number followed by the word heading.

marktripy.__version__ comes from the file marktripy/_version.py, which the build writes from the Git tag (via hatch-vcs). In a source checkout that has never been built, the file is missing and __version__ falls back to 0.0.0.

docs.title: Install from source
docs.text:
Prerequisites: Git and uv.

  1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/vexyart/vexy-marktripy
cd vexy-marktripy

  2. Create the environment and install the package in editable mode with its development tools:

    uv sync --dev

  3. Run the tests to confirm the checkout works:

    uv run pytest -q

The dev dependency group adds pytest, pytest-benchmark, pytest-cov, hypothesis, mypy, ruff, black, twine and hatch. See Contributing for the test and build commands.

docs.title: Turn on logging
docs.text:
Every module logs through loguru, but marktripy/__init__.py calls logger.disable("marktripy"), so nothing is printed by default. To see the debug messages while you work:

from loguru import logger

logger.enable("marktripy")

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text: These behaviours were confirmed by running the current code. Each entry says what happens and what to do instead.

docs.title: ImportError: cannot import name 'parse_markdown'
docs.text:
The README examples use parse_markdown, render_markdown, markdown_to_html, create_extension and a Parser(extensions=…) constructor. None of these exist. Use the module-level classes:

README name Use instead parse_markdown(text) ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it").parse(text) render_markdown(ast) MarkdownRenderer().render(ast) markdown_to_html(text) HTMLRenderer().render(ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it").parse(text)) create_extension(…) Subclass Extension; see Extensions

docs.title: No command-line tool
docs.text: The README shows marktripy convert, marktripy transform and marktripy validate. There is no CLI module, and the package installs no marktripy command.

docs.title: Parser 'mistletoe' not registered
docs.text: ParserRegistry only knows a parser after its module is imported. Add from marktripy.parsers import mistletoe_parser (or markdown_it) before calling ParserRegistry.create. The same applies to RendererRegistry and the modules in marktripy.renderers.

docs.title: Tables are not recognised
docs.text: The markdown-it adapter uses the commonmark preset by default, which has no table syntax. Pass {"preset": "default"}.

docs.title: Table body rows end up outside the table
docs.text:
With the markdown-it adapter, only the header row is placed inside the Table node. The body rows are added as siblings after the table. As a result:

  • MarkdownRenderer writes the header and separator but no body rows.
  • HTMLRenderer writes the body rows as bare <tr> elements after </table>.

The mistletoe adapter builds tables correctly (header and body inside Table), but has the other gaps listed below.

docs.title: mistletoe adapter gaps
docs.text:
• Fenced code blocks and strikethrough are dropped.
  • Any image raises ParserError: Failed to parse Markdown: 'Image' object has no attribute 'target'.
  • Column alignment is stored as mistletoe's numeric code, giving HTML such as align="1".

docs.title: Markdown output contains extra backslashes
docs.text: MarkdownRenderer escapes \ * _ ` [ ] ( ) # + - ! | { } in every text node regardless of context. well-known foo_bar (see #1) becomes well\-known foo\_bar \(see \#1\). The rendered result reads the same, but diffs against the source will show changes. See Renderers.

docs.title: The [[TOC]] marker is not replaced
docs.text: TOCGenerator is meant to replace a paragraph containing only the marker with the TOC. The parent lookup it uses never finds the paragraph, so the TOC is always inserted at the default position and the marker paragraph stays (escaped as \[\[TOC\]\] in Markdown output). Remove the marker paragraph yourself before or after running the generator.

docs.title: Reference definitions are escaped
docs.text: LinkReferenceTransformer appends definitions such as [1]: https://python.org as text. MarkdownRenderer escapes them to \[1\]: https://python.org, which is not a valid definition, so the [text][1] links in the output do not resolve.

docs.title: Hard line breaks become soft
docs.text: The markdown-it adapter converts both soft and hard breaks into Text("\n"). A line ending in two spaces loses its hard break in both Markdown and HTML output.

docs.title: Raw HTML is escaped in HTML output
docs.text: Inline and block HTML in the source become Text nodes. HTMLRenderer escapes them, so <b>x</b> appears as literal text <b>x</b>.

docs.title: Code blocks carry a language attribute in HTML
docs.text:
CodeBlock copies its language into attrs, and HTMLRenderer writes all attributes, so the output is <code language="python" class="language-python">. Remove it before rendering if you need clean HTML:

for block in doc.find_all("code_block"):
    block.attrs.pop("language", None)

docs.title: ++Ctrl+C++ is not a keyboard key
docs.text: KbdExtension does not allow + inside a key. Write ++Ctrl++ + ++C++.

docs.title: Ignored configuration keys
docs.text: These keys are read and stored but have no effect: MarkdownRenderer preserve_format; HTMLRenderer linkify and quotes; TOCGenerator indent_size and (because of the issue above) marker. Misspelt keys are ignored without an error.

docs.title: Parsers
docs.text:
A parser takes a Markdown string and returns a Document. Two adapters ship with the package:

Registry name Class Module Built on markdown-it MarkdownItParser marktripy.parsers.markdown_it markdown-it-py mistletoe MistletoeParser marktripy.parsers.mistletoe_parser mistletoe

Use markdown-it unless you have a reason not to. It is the adapter the test suite exercises most, and it is the only one that takes configuration. The mistletoe adapter drops several constructs; see The mistletoe adapter.

docs.title: Create a parser
docs.text:
Each adapter module registers itself with ParserRegistry when it is imported. Nothing is registered until then.

from marktripy.core.parser import ParserRegistry
from marktripy.parsers import markdown_it, mistletoe_parser  # both register now

print(ParserRegistry.list_parsers())   # ['markdown-it', 'mistletoe']

parser = ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it", {"preset": "default"})

ParserRegistry.create(name, config=None) looks up the class and calls it with config. If the name is unknown, ParserRegistry.get raises KeyError and lists the names that are registered, for example Parser 'mistletoe' not registered. Available: ['markdown-it'] when you forgot the import.

Constructing the class directly works the same way:

from marktripy.parsers.markdown_it import MarkdownItParser

parser = MarkdownItParser({"preset": "default"})

docs.title: What parse() does
docs.text:
parse(text) runs three steps:

  1. preprocess(text) converts \r\n and \r line endings to \n and adds a final newline if missing.
  2. The backend parses the text, and the adapter converts the backend's tokens into ASTNode objects.
  3. postprocess(doc) returns the document. The base implementation does not change it; subclasses can override it.

Any exception raised inside parse() is re-raised as ParserError with the message Failed to parse Markdown: <original message>. The original exception is available as __cause__. ParserError also has line and column attributes, but the shipped adapters do not set them.

validate_markdown(text) calls parse() and returns a list with the error message if parsing fails, or an empty list if it succeeds.

docs.title: The markdown-it adapter
docs.text:
MarkdownItParser accepts a configuration dictionary with these keys:

Key Default Effect preset "commonmark" markdown-it-py preset name: "commonmark", "default" or "zero". options {} Options passed to MarkdownIt(preset, options), for example {"typographer": True}. plugins [] Plugin names to load from mdit_py_plugins: front_matter, footnote, deflist, tasklists, attrs. Unknown names are logged and skipped. disable [] Rule names passed to md.disable(). enable [] Rule names passed to md.enable().

The adapter always enables the html_inline and html_block rules unless options["html"] is False.

docs.title: Choose a preset
docs.text:
The preset decides which syntax is recognised. The commonmark default does not recognise tables or ~~strikethrough~~. Use "default" for those:

ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it").get_capabilities()["tables"]                         # False
ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it", {"preset": "default"}).get_capabilities()["tables"]  # True

docs.title: Token mapping
docs.text:
The adapter maps markdown-it-py tokens to nodes as follows:

Token Node heading_open Heading(level=…) from the tag (h2 → 2) paragraph_open Paragraph blockquote_open BlockQuote hr HorizontalRule fence, code_block CodeBlock(content, language=info) bullet_list_open / ordered_list_open List(ordered=…, start=…, tight=…) list_item_open ListItem em_open, strong_open Emphasis, Strong s_open a plain ASTNode(type="strikethrough") link_open Link(href, title) image Image(src, alt, title) code_inline InlineCode text Text softbreak, hardbreak Text("\n") html_inline, html_block Text holding the raw HTML table_open, tr_open, th_open/td_open Table, TableRow, TableCell(header=…, align=…)

Tokens not in this list are skipped. Two consequences:

  • Raw HTML becomes ordinary text. HTMLRenderer escapes it, so <b>x</b> in the source becomes <b>x</b> in the output.
  • A hard line break (two trailing spaces) becomes the same Text("\n") as a soft break, so it renders as a plain newline.

docs.title: Plugins
docs.text:
Plugins add syntax to the tokenizer, but the adapter only converts the token types listed above. For example, with {"plugins": ["front_matter"]} the front matter block is recognised and then skipped, so it does not appear in the tree:

p = ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it", {"plugins": ["front_matter"]})
[n.type for n in p.parse("---
title: x
---

# H
").walk()]
# ['document', 'heading', 'text']

docs.title: The mistletoe adapter
docs.text:
MistletoeParser takes no configuration keys. It calls mistletoe.Document(text) and converts headings, paragraphs, lists, code blocks, quotes, tables, emphasis, strong, inline code and links.

With mistletoe 1.6 the adapter has these gaps:

  • Fenced code blocks (```) and ~~strikethrough~~ are dropped from the tree with a logged warning. Indented code blocks are converted.
  • Any image makes parse() fail with ParserError: Failed to parse Markdown: 'Image' object has no attribute 'target'.
  • Table column alignment is copied as mistletoe's numeric code instead of "left", "center" or "right". A right-aligned column, for example, produces align="1" in HTML.

Prefer the markdown-it adapter for real documents until these are fixed.

docs.title: Capabilities
docs.text:
get_capabilities() returns a dictionary of feature flags: tables, strikethrough, task_lists, footnotes, definition_lists, math, smart_quotes and custom_extensions.

For MarkdownItParser the values are computed from the active markdown-it-py rules, so they change with the preset and plugins. For MistletoeParser they are fixed values and do not reflect the gaps listed above.

docs.title: Write your own adapter
docs.text:
Subclass Parser, implement parse() and get_capabilities(), and register the class:

from marktripy.core.ast import Document, Paragraph, Text
from marktripy.core.parser import Parser, ParserRegistry


class PlainTextParser(Parser):
    """Treat every blank-line-separated block as a paragraph."""

    def parse(self, text: str) -> Document:
        doc = Document()
        for block in self.preprocess(text).split("\n\n"):
            if block.strip():
                para = Paragraph()
                para.add_child(Text(block.strip()))
                doc.add_child(para)
        return self.postprocess(doc)

    def get_capabilities(self) -> dict[str, bool]:
        return {"tables": False, "custom_extensions": False}


ParserRegistry.register("plain", PlainTextParser)

ParserRegistry.register raises TypeError if the class is not a Parser subclass. Registering an existing name replaces the earlier class.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
This page follows one small document through a parse, two changes and two renders. Every output shown was produced by running the code against the current source.

Prerequisite: marktripy is installed (Installation).

docs.title: 1. Create a parser
docs.text:
Parsers are registered by name when their module is imported. Import the module, then ask the registry for an instance:

from marktripy.core.parser import ParserRegistry
from marktripy.parsers import markdown_it  # registers "markdown-it"

parser = ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it")

You can also construct the class directly: markdown_it.MarkdownItParser().

docs.title: 2. Parse Markdown
docs.text:
doc = parser.parse("# Hello\n\nThis is **bold** text.\n")

doc is a Document node. Its tree looks like this:

document
  heading            level=1
    text             'Hello'
  paragraph
    text             'This is '
    strong
      text           'bold'
    text             ' text.'

Inline formatting is a node with children: **bold** became a strong node that contains a text node.

docs.title: 3. Change the tree
docs.text:
Every node has walk() (all nodes, depth first) and find_all(type) (all nodes of one type). Headings carry their level in the level attribute:

for heading in doc.find_all("heading"):
    heading.level += 1

The Heading constructor rejects levels outside 1–6, but assigning level afterwards is not checked. The transformers in Transformers clamp levels for you.

docs.title: 4. Render Markdown
docs.text:
from marktripy.renderers.markdown import MarkdownRenderer

print(MarkdownRenderer().render(doc))

Output:

## Hello

This is **bold** text.

docs.title: 5. Render HTML
docs.text:
from marktripy.renderers.html import HTMLRenderer

print(HTMLRenderer().render(doc))

Output:

<h2>Hello</h2>
<p>This is <strong>bold</strong> text.</p>

docs.title: 6. Add heading IDs and a table of contents
docs.text:
The transformer modules provide one-call helper functions.

from marktripy.transformers.id_generator import add_heading_ids
from marktripy.transformers.toc import generate_toc

doc = parser.parse("# Intro\n\n## Setup\n\n## Setup\n\n### Café & Crème\n")
add_heading_ids(doc)            # changes doc in place
doc = generate_toc(doc)         # returns a new Document with the TOC inserted

print(MarkdownRenderer().render(doc))

Output:

# Intro

## Table of Contents

- [Intro](#intro)
   - [Setup](#setup)
   - [Setup](#setup-1)
      - [Café & Crème](#cafe-creme)

## Setup

## Setup

### Café & Crème

What happened:

  • add_heading_ids slugified each heading's text. The second Setup got the suffix -1 so IDs stay unique, and the accents were stripped (Café & Crème → cafe-creme).
  • generate_toc collected headings of levels 1–3, built a nested list of links, and inserted it after the first level-1 heading. It returned a copy of the document, so keep the return value.

The IDs are stored in each heading's attrs and appear in HTML output (<h2 id="setup">Setup</h2>). Markdown has no heading-ID syntax, so MarkdownRenderer does not write them.

docs.title: 7. Enable GFM features
docs.text:
Strikethrough and task lists need two things: a parser preset that recognises the syntax, and the extension that turns the parsed result into proper nodes and renders them.

from marktripy.extensions.base import ExtensionManager
from marktripy.extensions.gfm import GFMExtension

parser = ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it", {"preset": "default"})
html = HTMLRenderer()

manager = ExtensionManager()
manager.register(GFMExtension())
manager.apply_renderer_extensions(html, "html")

doc = parser.parse("~~old~~ new\n\n- [ ] todo\n- [x] done\n")
doc = manager.apply_ast_transformations(doc)
print(html.render(doc))

Output (line breaks as produced):

<p><del>old</del> new</p>
<ul>
<li><input type="checkbox" disabled> todo</li><li><input type="checkbox" disabled checked> done</li></ul>

See Extensions for the order of these calls and for the ++key++ extension.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• The AST lists every node class and tree method.
  • Parsers explains presets, plugins and the mistletoe adapter.
  • Known limitations lists the cases that do not round-trip yet.

docs.title: Renderers
docs.text:
A renderer turns a Document into a string. Two renderers ship with the package and register themselves when their module is imported:

Registry name Class Module Output markdown MarkdownRenderer marktripy.renderers.markdown Markdown html HTMLRenderer marktripy.renderers.html HTML fragment (no <html> or <body>) 
from marktripy.renderers.base import RendererRegistry
from marktripy.renderers import html, markdown  # registers "html" and "markdown"

renderer = RendererRegistry.create("markdown", {"bullet_char": "*"})

Constructing the class directly is equivalent: MarkdownRenderer({"bullet_char": "*"}).

docs.title: How rendering works
docs.text:
render(ast) resets the render context and calls render_node(ast). render_node looks up a method named render_<node.type> on the renderer and calls it. Each method renders its children by calling render_node again, so the whole tree is visited depth first.

If no method matches, render_unknown runs:

  • MarkdownRenderer logs a warning and outputs nothing for that node.
  • HTMLRenderer logs a warning and outputs <!-- Unknown node type: <type> -->.

This lookup is also how extensions add output for new node types: they attach a render_<type> function to the renderer instance. You can do the same:

from marktripy.core.ast import ASTNode, Document
from marktripy.renderers.html import HTMLRenderer

html = HTMLRenderer()
html.render_callout = lambda node: f'<aside>{html.render_children(node)}</aside>\n'

doc = Document()
doc.add_child(ASTNode(type="callout", children=[]))
print(html.render(doc))   # <aside></aside>

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
Key Default Effect heading_style "atx" "setext" writes level 1 and 2 headings with === / --- underlines. Levels 3–6 always use #. emphasis_char "*" Delimiter for emphasis nodes, for example "_". strong_char "**" Delimiter for strong nodes, for example "__". bullet_char "-" Marker for unordered list items. code_fence "`" Character repeated three times to fence code blocks. "~" gives ~~~. line_width 0 If greater than 0, paragraph text is re-wrapped at this width. 0 means no wrapping. preserve_format False Stored on the renderer but not used by any method. indent " " Used by get_indent(). List rendering uses a fixed three-space continuation indent instead.

Example with non-default options:

from marktripy.core.parser import ParserRegistry
from marktripy.parsers import markdown_it
from marktripy.renderers.markdown import MarkdownRenderer

doc = ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it").parse("# Title\n\n*it* and\n\n- a\n")
r = MarkdownRenderer({"heading_style": "setext", "emphasis_char": "_", "bullet_char": "*"})
print(r.render(doc))

Output:

Title
=====

_it_ and

* a

docs.title: Output rules
docs.text:
• Blocks in the document are separated by one blank line. The output always ends with exactly one newline.
  • Ordered lists are numbered from List.start (or 1) and counted up, so 3. x / 4. y round-trips.
  • Code blocks use a fence of three code_fence characters, or four if the content already contains three. The language follows the opening fence.
  • Inline code uses enough backticks to enclose any backticks in the content.
  • A Link with a reference_id attribute is written as [text][id]. Otherwise it is written inline, with the title in quotes if set.
  • Tables are written with padded columns and a separator row that shows alignment (:--, --:, :-:). The first row is treated as the header if all its cells have header=True.
  • HorizontalRule is always written as ---.

docs.title: Escaping
docs.text:
render_text escapes these characters with a backslash in every text node: \ * _ ` [ ] ( ) # + - ! | { }. It does this without looking at context, so plain prose picks up escapes that a person would not write:

doc = ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it").parse("Use the well-known foo_bar (see #1).\n")
print(MarkdownRenderer().render(doc))
# Use the well\-known foo\_bar \(see \#1\).

The escaped Markdown renders to the same text, but it is not byte-for-byte what you parsed. Text inside inline_code and code_block nodes is not escaped.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
The option names follow markdown-it conventions.

Key Default Effect xhtml False Writes <hr /> and <img … /> instead of <hr> and <img …>. breaks False Replaces each newline inside a text node with <br> plus a newline. langPrefix "language-" Prefix for the class added to code blocks with a language. typographer False Replaces -- with an em dash (—) and ... with an ellipsis (…) in text nodes. Quote replacement is not implemented. quotes '""' + "''" Stored but unused, because quote replacement is not implemented. linkify False Stored but unused.

Example:

from marktripy.renderers.html import HTMLRenderer

doc = ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it").parse("a -- b...\nline2\n\n---\n")
print(HTMLRenderer({"xhtml": True, "typographer": True, "breaks": True}).render(doc))

Output:

<p>a — b…<br>
line2</p>
<hr />

docs.title: Output rules
docs.text:
• Text, code, link href/title and image src/alt/title are escaped with html.escape(…, quote=True).
  • Every entry in a node's attrs becomes an HTML attribute. True writes the bare attribute name; False and None are skipped; other values are converted to strings and escaped. Heading IDs therefore appear as <h2 id="setup">.
  • Because CodeBlock stores its language in attrs too, a fenced block produces both a language attribute and a class: <pre><code language="python" class="language-python">.
  • Ordered lists with a start other than 1 get a start attribute.
  • In tight lists, a list item that renders as a single <p>…</p> has the paragraph tags removed.
  • Table cells with an alignment get both align="…" (from attrs) and style="text-align: …;".
  • Empty paragraphs produce no output.

docs.title: Write your own renderer
docs.text:
Subclass Renderer and implement render() and render_node(). The base class provides render_children(), escape() (returns the text unchanged) and get_indent().

from marktripy.core.ast import ASTNode, Document
from marktripy.renderers.base import Renderer, RendererRegistry


class PlainTextRenderer(Renderer):
    """Output only the text content, one block per line."""

    def render(self, ast: Document) -> str:
        return "\n".join(self.render_node(child) for child in ast.children) + "\n"

    def render_node(self, node: ASTNode) -> str:
        if node.content is not None:
            return node.content
        return self.render_children(node)


RendererRegistry.register("plain", PlainTextRenderer)

RenderContext (in marktripy.renderers.base) holds per-render state that the shipped renderers use: list_depth, tight_list, in_table, in_code_block, plus set_data() / get_data() for your own values. Both shipped renderers create a fresh context at the start of every render() call and store it in self.context.

docs.title: Transformers
docs.text:
A transformer takes a Document, changes it, and returns a Document. The package ships four, each with helper functions for one-line use.

Module Classes Helper functions marktripy.transformers.heading HeadingLevelTransformer, HeadingShifter, HeadingNormalizer increase_heading_levels, decrease_heading_levels, normalize_headings marktripy.transformers.id_generator IDGeneratorTransformer, HeadingIDGenerator, TableIDGenerator add_heading_ids, add_ids_to_elements marktripy.transformers.toc TOCGenerator generate_toc, extract_toc marktripy.transformers.link_reference LinkReferenceTransformer, LinkCollector convert_to_reference_links, collect_links

Always keep the return value

Most transformers change the tree in place and return the same object. TOCGenerator with insertion enabled returns a copy with the TOC added and leaves the input unchanged. Write doc = transformer.transform(doc) every time and you do not need to remember which is which.

The examples on this page use this setup:

from marktripy.core.parser import ParserRegistry
from marktripy.parsers import markdown_it
from marktripy.renderers.markdown import MarkdownRenderer

parser = ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it")
md = MarkdownRenderer()

docs.title: Heading levels
docs.text:
HeadingLevelTransformer(config) changes every heading's level. Configuration keys:

Key Default Meaning operation "increase" "increase", "decrease", "set" or "normalize" amount 1 Step for increase and decrease level 1 Target level for set min_level 1 Lowest allowed result max_level 6 Highest allowed result

Every result is clamped to min_level…max_level, so increasing a level 6 heading leaves it at 6.

normalize maps the distinct levels in use, in order, to 1, 2, 3…:

from marktripy.transformers.heading import normalize_headings

doc = parser.parse("### A\n\n##### B\n\n### C\n")
normalize_headings(doc)
print(md.render(doc))

Output:

# A

## B

# C

The levels 3 and 5 became 1 and 2. Gaps disappear, but the relative order is kept.

Shortcuts:

  • HeadingShifter(shift) increases for a positive shift and decreases for a negative one.
  • HeadingNormalizer() is HeadingLevelTransformer({"operation": "normalize"}).
  • increase_heading_levels(ast, amount=1) and decrease_heading_levels(ast, amount=1) build the transformer and run it.

docs.title: Heading IDs
docs.text:
IDGeneratorTransformer(config) stores a unique id attribute on matching nodes. Configuration keys:

Key Default Meaning prefix "" Text prepended to the heading text before slugifying, joined with separator separator "-" Joiner between prefix and the text overwrite False Replace IDs that are already present target_elements ["heading"] Node types that receive IDs

The ID is built by generate_id() from marktripy.utils.slugify:

  1. Extract the node's plain text (Café & Crème).
  2. Normalise to ASCII, lower-case, drop everything except letters, digits, spaces and hyphens (cafe creme).
  3. Collapse runs of spaces and hyphens into - (cafe-creme).
  4. If the slug is empty, use section. If it is already used in this document, append -1, -2, … until it is unique.

When overwrite is False, IDs already in the tree are collected first, so new IDs never collide with them.

from marktripy.transformers.id_generator import add_heading_ids

doc = parser.parse("# Intro\n\n## Setup\n\n## Setup\n")
add_heading_ids(doc, prefix="doc")
print([h.get_attr("id") for h in doc.find_all("heading")])
# ['doc-intro', 'doc-setup', 'doc-setup-1']

HeadingIDGenerator(prefix="", overwrite=False) targets headings only. TableIDGenerator(prefix="table", overwrite=False) targets tables. Tables have no text of their own, so a table's ID is built from the joined text of the cells inside the Table node: header cells a and b give table-ab. add_ids_to_elements(ast, elements, prefix="", overwrite=False) lets you pass any list of node types.

The IDs appear in HTML output. MarkdownRenderer ignores them because Markdown has no heading-ID syntax.

docs.title: Table of contents
docs.text:
TOCGenerator(config) collects headings and builds a nested list of links. Configuration keys:

Key Default Meaning min_level 1 Lowest heading level to include max_level 3 Highest heading level to include title "Table of Contents" Text of a level 2 heading placed above the list. An empty string omits it. insert True Insert the TOC into a copy of the document ordered False Use ordered lists instead of bullet lists marker "[[TOC]]" Paragraph text to replace with the TOC. See the note below. indent_size 2 Stored but not used

Each entry links to #<id> if the heading has an id attribute, and is plain text otherwise. Run the ID transformer first if you want links.

Where the TOC goes: directly after the first level 1 heading at the top of the document, or before the first other block. Paragraphs that start with --- or +++ are skipped over.

Marker replacement does not take effect

The code looks for a paragraph whose only text is the marker, but its parent lookup never finds the paragraph, so the marker is left in place and the TOC is inserted at the default position. With MarkdownRenderer the leftover marker is then escaped as \[\[TOC\]\]. Remove the marker paragraph yourself if you use one. See Known limitations.

Chain IDs and the TOC:

from marktripy.transformers.base import TransformerChain
from marktripy.transformers.id_generator import HeadingIDGenerator
from marktripy.transformers.toc import TOCGenerator

doc = parser.parse("# Guide\n\n## Install\n\n## Use\n\n### Detail\n")
chain = TransformerChain([
    HeadingIDGenerator(prefix="doc"),
    TOCGenerator({"title": "Contents", "max_level": 2}),
])
print(md.render(chain.transform(doc)))

Output:

# Guide

## Contents

- [Guide](#doc-guide)
   - [Install](#doc-install)
   - [Use](#doc-use)

## Install

## Use

### Detail

generate_toc(ast, max_level=3, insert=True) and extract_toc(ast, max_level=3) are shortcuts. extract_toc returns the TOC as a Document node (title heading plus list) without changing the input, or None if there are no headings in range. After any run, TOCGenerator.get_toc() returns the same node.

docs.title: Reference-style links
docs.text:
LinkReferenceTransformer(config) gives every inline link a reference ID and appends the definitions at the end of the document. Configuration keys:

Key Default Meaning style "numeric" "numeric" gives 1, 2, …; "text" slugifies the link text (up to 50 characters) dedup True Reuse one ID for links with the same URL section_title "References" Level 2 heading above the definitions. An empty string omits it. preserve_titles True Keep link titles in the definitions

The transformer sets attrs["reference_id"] on each Link. MarkdownRenderer then writes the link as [text][id]. The definitions are added as paragraphs containing text such as [1]: https://python.org.

Definitions are escaped in Markdown output

The definitions are plain Text nodes, so MarkdownRenderer escapes their brackets: \[1\]: https://python.org. The result is not a valid reference definition. See Known limitations.

collect_links(ast) returns all Link nodes without changing anything:

from marktripy.transformers.link_reference import collect_links

doc = parser.parse('See [Python](https://python.org) and [docs](https://python.org "Py").\n')
print([link.href for link in collect_links(doc)])
# ['https://python.org', 'https://python.org']

docs.title: Write your own transformer
docs.text:
Subclass Transformer, implement get_description(), and add visit_<type> methods for the node types you care about.

How the traversal works:

  1. transform(ast) calls visit(ast).
  2. visit(node) calls visit_<node.type> if it exists, otherwise generic_visit(node).
  3. generic_visit(node) visits each child and keeps the returned node. A child whose visit returns None is removed.
  4. If your visit_<type> method should also process the node's children, call self.generic_visit(node) inside it.

This transformer removes all images and upper-cases link text:

from marktripy.transformers.base import Transformer


class Tidy(Transformer):
    def get_description(self) -> str:
        return "Remove images, upper-case link text"

    def visit_image(self, node):
        return None                      # drop the node

    def visit_text(self, node):
        if self.config.get("in_link"):
            node.content = node.content.upper()
        return node

    def visit_link(self, node):
        self.config["in_link"] = True
        self.generic_visit(node)
        self.config["in_link"] = False
        return node


doc = Tidy().transform(parser.parse("![x](a.png) see [the docs](https://example.com)\n"))
print(md.render(doc))

Output:

 see [THE DOCS](https://example.com)

TransformerChain(transformers) runs a list of transformers in order and has add_transformer() and remove_transformer(). TransformerRegistry offers register(), get(), create(), list_transformers() and create_chain(names, configs=None), but none of the shipped transformers register themselves, so you must register any you want to create by name.

docs.title: Validate a tree
docs.text:
marktripy.core.validator checks that a tree has a sensible structure. It is useful after you build or edit a tree by hand, before you render it.

from marktripy.core.ast import Document, List, Paragraph, Text
from marktripy.core.validator import validate_ast

doc = Document()
doc.add_child(Text("loose"))          # inline node directly under the document
bad_list = List()
bad_list.add_child(Paragraph())       # list that contains a paragraph
doc.add_child(bad_list)

for error in validate_ast(doc):
    print(error)

Output:

Document contains inline element at text node
List contains non-list-item: paragraph at paragraph node

Each error is a ValidationError (a subclass of Exception). Its message ends with at <type> node, and its node attribute holds the node that failed.

docs.title: Entry points
docs.text: Call Result validate_ast(ast, strict=False) Returns a list of ValidationError; empty if the tree is valid. validate_ast_strict(ast) Runs strict validation and raises the first error. ASTValidator(strict=False).validate(ast) Same as validate_ast. The errors are also kept in validator.errors. ASTValidator(strict=…).validate_strict(ast) Validates and raises the first error, if any. Despite the name, it uses the validator's own strict setting.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
The validator visits every node and calls _validate_<type> for it.

Node type Always checked Checked only with strict=True document No direct text, emphasis, strong or inline_code children — heading Level is 1–6; has children or content — list Only list_item children; ordered start is not negative — list_item — Not empty link href is not empty Has text image src is not empty; has no children — table Only table_row children; all rows have the same number of cells — table_row Only table_cell children — blockquote — Not empty any other type — Logs a warning (not an error)

Example: a link with an empty target, as parsed from [x]():

from marktripy.core.parser import ParserRegistry
from marktripy.parsers import markdown_it

doc = ParserRegistry.create("markdown-it").parse("# ok\n\n[x]()\n")
print(validate_ast(doc))
# [ValidationError('Link has no href at link node')]

docs.title: Slugs and IDs
docs.text: marktripy.utils.slugify contains the text helpers the transformers use. You can call them directly.

docs.title: slugify(text, lowercase=True, separator="-", max_length=None, allowed_chars=None)
docs.text:
Converts text to a URL-friendly slug in five steps: NFKD-normalise and drop non-ASCII, optionally lower-case, remove characters other than letters, digits, whitespace, hyphens and allowed_chars, collapse whitespace and hyphen runs into separator, strip separator from the ends. If max_length is set, the result is cut to that length and trailing separators are removed.

from marktripy.utils.slugify import slugify

slugify("Hello, World! Café")             # 'hello-world-cafe'
slugify("Hello World", separator="_")     # 'hello_world'
slugify("v1.2 notes", allowed_chars=".")  # 'v1.2-notes'

docs.title: generate_id(text, existing_ids=None)
docs.text:
Slugifies text and makes it unique against the set existing_ids by appending -1, -2, …. An empty slug becomes section. The function does not add the result to the set.

from marktripy.utils.slugify import generate_id

generate_id("Intro", {"intro"})   # 'intro-1'
generate_id("!!!")                # 'section'

docs.title: IDGenerator(prefix="", separator="-")
docs.text: A stateful wrapper around generate_id. generate(text) prepends prefix + separator when a prefix is set, returns a unique ID and remembers it in used_ids. has_id(value) checks whether an ID was issued; reset() forgets them all.

docs.title: extract_text(node)
docs.text: Returns the plain text of a node: its content if set, otherwise the concatenated text of its children. Formatting is dropped, so **bold** text gives bold text.
